sentences.text: 2. By the impugned award, against a claim of Rs. 15,84,000/-, the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 5,46,600/- on account of death of deceased Lalu Sajan Kumar in an accident that occurred on 01.01.2015 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle Trailer bearing registration No. CG 15 AC 0813 driven by the respondent No. 1/Ravishankar Jaiswal, owned by respondent No.2/ Smt. Sumandeep Singh and insured with respondent No.3/ United India Insurance Company.
3. As per the pleadings of the claim application filed under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, the deceased was aged about 19 years, he was working as Labour and was earning Rs. 8,000/- per month.

4. The claim application was resisted by respondents No.1 & 2 and denied the averments of the claim application Neutral Citation and pleaded that in the event of liability was found, the same should be on the Insurance Company.
5. The Insurance Company also filed its written statement and denied the averments of the claim application and pleaded that the offending vehicle was being driven without any valid and effective driving license and also was not having valid fitness and permit, therefore, the Insurance Company may be exonerated.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants submits that the income of the deceased has been taken on the lower side, future prospect is also not awarded and compensation on all other heads is also on the lower side.

In support of above contention, reliance has been placed on the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matters of Smt. Sarla Verma and others VS. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the record.

8. As per pleadings of the appellants / claimants the deceased was working as a (Labour) Supervisor and he was earning Rs. 8,000/- per month but to prudent and Neutral Citation cogent evidence was brought on record.
However, looking to the date of accident, numbers of dependents, nature of job and prevailing minimum wages, this Court holds that the deceased was earning Rs. 5,500/- per month.

Taking guidance from the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma & Pranay Sethi (supra), and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors; (2018)
18 SCC 130 this Court computes the compensation in the following manner:-
 S. No. Description Amount  1. Monthly income 5500/-
 2. 40% Future prospect 2200/-
 3. Total Monthly Income (5500+2200) 7,700/-
 4. Total Yearly Income (7700x12) 92,400/-

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6 . Net income 46,200/-
7. Multiplier of 18 applied to assess 8,31,600/-
total loss of dependency 8.

Funeral Expenses 15,000/-
9. Loss of estate 15,000/-
10.
Filial consortium 80,000/-

Total compensation 9,41,600/-
 Neutral Citation 9.
For the forgoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.

The amount of compensation of Rs.
5,46,000/- awarded by learned tribunal is enhanced to Rs. 9,41,600/-.

Hence, after deducting the amount of Rs. 5,46,000/-, the claimants are held entitled for an additional amount of Rs.
3,95,600/-.
The additional amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the appeal i.e. 02.01.2017.
The impugned award stands modified to the above extent.
10. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of compensation within 60 days.

Out of total amount deposit, 45%-45% (each) shall be invested as fixed deposit in a nationalized bank for a period of three years in the name of appellants and remaining amount shall be paid to appellant No. 1 through bank transaction/account payee cheque.
11. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part.
12. No cost.
